newsitem.title: USA: Delta Air and Continental in merger talks - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Delta Air and Continental in merger talks - NYT.

text.p: Delta Air Lines and Continental Airlines are in talks about a possible merger, The New York Times reported Wednesday, citing sources familiar with the discussions.
Though no deal is imminent, the Times story said, the talks have been going on for several months and have moved beyond preliminary stages.
Continental, which initiated the discussions, is not talking to any other airline about a possible merger, the story said.
The combination of Delta, the nation's third-largest airline, and Continental, the fifth largest, would create the world's biggest airline. United Airlines is currently the world's largest.

The Times' story quoted Standard & Poor's airline industry analyst Philip Baggaley as saying a merger of this size would probably lead to several other combinations as airlines scramble for merger partners to avoid being marginalized.
Spokesmen for the two airlines declined to comment in the Times' story.
